subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@finsecure.com>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finsecure.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation questions

Hi Paul / Leah,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about FinSecure's use cases and the data isolation needs you flagged. Quick recap from my side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can loop in the right folks on our side: 

- Current requirement you emphasized: customer data must not leave your cloud tenancy or be processed on multi-tenant shared hosters (regulatory constraint + internal policy).
- You're evaluating two deployment modes: Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools) vs Private VPC/on-prem (customer-managed network).

Clarifying questions: 
1) For Dedicated, would FinSecure consider a model where inference runs on isolated GPUs in our Dedicated fleet but network egress and logs are retained by Redwood by default? Or do you require that all inference traffic and logs remain inside your VPC (i.e., Private VPC or on-prem only)?
2) Do you have an existing KMS/HSM integration requirement (bring-your-own-key) for model input/output encryption at rest?
3) What compliance evidence will your security/compliance team need to accept a Dedicated deployment vs requiring Private? Examples: SOC 2, network diagrams showing no internet egress, or continuous audit logs.

I've attached a short one-pager summarizing the three deployment options and a SOC2 summary we discussed. If you're open, I can set up a 30-min call next week with Dylan (solutions engineer) to walk through network diagrams and what we can lock down for Dedicated.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm whether Dedicated is on the table subject to additional controls, or if Private VPC/on-prem is the only acceptable route.
- If Dedicated is acceptable, we'll schedule a technical deep-dive (Dylan) to review network controls and logging retention.

Thanks — look forward to your guidance so we can scope appropriately.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation questions

Marissa — thanks for the recap. A couple quick answers from our side: 

- High level: FinSecure's security policy prefers customer-controlled network boundaries. Private VPC or on-prem is the cleanest path for our legal/compliance team.
- That said, Dedicated could be considered if you can provide: 
  * Proof that inference traffic never leaves our tenancy or is available to other tenants (network isolation guarantee),
  * BYOK/KMS integration so keys never reside on Redwood-managed HSMs, and
  * Audit logs (request/response) retained in our account for 7 years.

Can Dylan join a technical call next week to walk through what Dedicated could lock down? If not feasible, we'll likely request a Private VPC evaluation.

Paul
Paul Henderson
Head of IT Security, FinSecure
paul.henderson@finsecure.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@finsecure.com>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finsecure.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation questions

Thanks Paul — really helpful detail. Looping in Dylan (solutions engineering) and Jordan (platform PM) to make sure we cover each bullet: 

Dylan / Jordan — FinSecure's asks if Dedicated is to remain an option:
- Network isolation guarantees: FinSecure needs confirmation that inference traffic (model inputs/outputs) would be processed in isolated compute (no sidecar tenants) and that there is no cross-customer egress. They also want a network topology diagram showing no public internet egress from inference nodes.
- BYOK/KMS: they want a BYOK flow where keys are customer-managed and not accessible by Redwood operators.
- Audit logs: they require request/response audit logs to be retained in their account for 7 years (or an agreed archival location under their control).

Dylan — can you confirm whether Redwood Dedicated can meet these three items with additional controls (e.g., private peering, customer KMS integration, log forwarding to customer S3/GCS)? If not fully possible, flag which elements would require Private VPC/on-prem.

If it helps, I'll propose two meeting options next week: 
- Option A: Dedicated deep-dive — tech call to validate isolation controls (30 min)
- Option B: Private VPC exploration — longer workshop (60 min) to scope on-prem/VPC network and install requirements.

Preferred next-step from FinSecure would be great.

Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: network-isolation-diagram.png]
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finsecure.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation questions

Paul / Leah — thanks — happy to take the deep-dive. Quick notes before the call so we can be efficient: 

1) Dedicated isolation: we can provision single-tenant GPU pools for your account and enforce private peering so inference traffic originates from your VPC and returns to it. That addresses the network boundary requirement in many cases. We'll walk through the exact peering/topology on the call.

2) BYOK/KMS: we support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping and can integrate with AWS KMS or customer HSM via standard APIs. We will not retain unwrapped keys on Redwood hosts. Exact HSM integrations depend on your provider — we'll list supported options in the call.

3) Audit logs: we can forward request/response logs and agent metrics to your S3/GCS bucket or to a SIEM via secure forwarding. Retention to 7 years is achievable; we'll outline the archive flow and access controls.

If the above sounds like it covers FinSecure's checklist, let's lock a 30-min slot this week for the Dedicated deep-dive (I can bring network/TLS folks). If any item is non-negotiable (e.g., absolutely no Redwood-managed compute allowed), we'll pivot to Private VPC/on-prem and I can scope that workshop too.

Proposed slots (PST): Tue 12/1 10:00-10:30, Wed 12/2 14:00-14:30. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
